newsitem.title: GERMANY: Viag wants telecoms break - even in 5 years.
newsitem.headline: Viag wants telecoms break - even in 5 years.

text.p: German industrial group Viag AG wants its telecommunications joint venture to break-even five years after it is launched following the liberalisation of the sector in 1998.

"It should be at break-even after five years from 1998," Viag management board chairman Georg Obermeier said at a dinner held for journalists in Frankfurt, adding that he meant by break-even that the business should "finance itself."
Obermeier repeated estimates that the alliance between Viag, British Telecom and Germany's RWE would invest between 4-5 billion marks over the five years.

Viag was "optimistic" that it and its partners would be awarded the fourth German mobile telephone licence -- for which the bidding deadline is mid-October -- as the consortium was the only confirmed bidder so far.
But Obermeier said that, if it was not granted the licence then it would have to revise its current plans.

Precise details of the three-way tie-up are due to be confirmed this autumn. It is expected that each partner will have a roughly equal share with a 5-8 percent stake left open to potential future partners.

He added that Viag's aim was that its share of telecom revenues would eventually bring in 10-15 percent of the energy-to-packaging concern's total turnover, which, measured at the group level, stood at 41.9 billion marks in 1995.

It would nonetheless take around two to three years after 1998, when European Union laws require Europe's telecom markets to be open to competition, before it had fully reached its potential customer base, Obermeier said.
The combination of telecom infrastructure already owned by Viag and RWE give the alliance a trunk network within reach of some 80 percent of the population.
